source.title: A Mechanistic Study of Algorithmic Generalization in Diffusion Models on Modular Arithmetic
source.authors: Joonkee Kim; Yong-Hyun Park; Mattis Dalsætra Østby; Jia-Tao Gu

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization on modular addition using image-generating flow-matching diffusion models, a different architecture and task representation from the cited token-based studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking trajectories, architecture and data-regime comparisons, Fourier analyses of the learned arithmetic computation, and timestep-wise rectification results. The latter measure behavior during sampling, not the training-time grokking delay. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper trains flow-matching diffusion transformers on image-based modular addition. It reports training and validation accuracy trajectories showing delayed generalization after overfitting. This is a test of V1 in a new model class and output modality (generating images, not predicting tokens). Its Fourier analysis is done on trained models only, not over training, so it does not test V2. It tracks no training-set size, weight-decay, initialization or optimizer variable, so V3, V5, V6 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors also explicitly leave open how broadly these mechanisms transfer beyond modular addition. They present the FFN-sandwich architecture as what enables arithmetic circuits in the diverse-image regime.
record.recipe_differences: Uses image-based modular addition and flow-matching DiT diffusion models that generate result images, rather than token-based discrete prediction. The training ratio is fixed at 0.9; visual diversity and patch size are varied.
record.method_sensitivity: Visual diversity changes the generalization lag: N = 4 has validation accuracy spike before training saturation, while N = 1 shows a prolonged delay. Smaller patch size prolongs overfitting. In the N = 256 regime, grokking depends on architecture: the standard SA–FFN model fails, while FFN-sandwich and depth-2 models grok.

fits_no_version.finding: Periodic operand representations at frequencies w1, w3, w7 and w9 compose in the FFN pre-GeLU activations into trigonometric addition identities (FVE 0.87–0.96).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An image-generating diffusion model trained on modular addition implements the sum through Fourier features and trigonometric composition, as token transformers do.

fits_no_version.finding: During sampling, rectification of incorrect result images fails beyond a timestep that the FVE entropy curvature predicts (R2 = 0.84). An inverse feature-volume metric predicts the same in a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM (median error 0.04).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal representation-structure measures predict when diffusion-model rectification fails during sampling.

record.problems: The training-set-size dependence in V1 is not tested. Several grokking trajectories are reported through figures without exact accuracy values or training-step counts. The N = 256 single-layer result reaches 94% terminal validation accuracy, and grokking fails for the standard SA–FFN architecture in that regime.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 repeats the Fourier expansion analysis in Table 1 with additional non-significant frequencies; it is omitted to avoid duplicating the same projected channels. Figures 6–7 and Appendices H–N provide additional sampling-time visualizations and configuration-specific transition results; they are not training-time grokking measurements and are not separately itemized here.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size. The training ratio is fixed at 0.9 throughout, and no delay is quantified in steps.
Fourier and circuit analysis is done only on final trained models. There is no tracking of circuit formation or of memorization removal across training, and no progress measures.
No grokking-delay test on non-algorithmic data; the CIFAR-10 EDM is a pretrained model used only for sampling-time rectification. No initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
AdamW is used but weight decay is not varied. No critical dataset size and no ungrokking.

A single trained run per setting is analyzed. Frequency sets differ between the single-image model (4 frequencies) and the diverse-image model (5 frequencies), but runs are not compared for algorithm identity.

missing.what: The authors state that the same qualitative grokking behavior holds across moduli P = 27, 31, 35 (EMNIST) and P = 39, 43, 47 (KMNIST). No row records this; the appendix figures shown focus on Fourier and transition structure.
Inference accuracy of 95% on the non-redundant N = 256 evaluation set, against the 94% terminal validation accuracy in r5.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed to T3: the study asks the same question, but in a new model class and output modality. The study is not one of the original sources. Grokking evidence comes only from figures, with no step counts or delay magnitudes. Training uses AdamW with a WSD learning-rate schedule; weight decay and the schedule's effect on the delay are not examined.

versions.untested_parts: Does not vary training-set size; the training ratio is fixed at 0.9. The results therefore do not test whether a smaller training set takes more optimization.
Does not track circuit formation or removal of memorizing components over training, or test whether training-time progress measures anticipate the generalization jump.
No grokking-delay test on non-algorithmic data, or initialization-scale or weight-norm intervention. CIFAR-10 analysis concerns rectification and feature-volume timing, not grokking.
No test of weight decay or low-norm bias as an efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs or test convergence to the same algorithm.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities, softmax numerical limits, or whether controlling them removes grokking.

rows.subject: single-layer DiT
rows.operation_detail: Train on image-based modular addition, then track training and validation accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over training
rows.value: Training accuracy rises rapidly while validation accuracy remains near chance for an extended period; after prolonged overfitting, validation accuracy transitions sharply to near-perfect generalization.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes the delayed transition after training accuracy rises; exact accuracy values and step counts are not stated.

rows.subject: single-layer DiT
rows.operation_detail: Train on image-based modular addition with increased visual diversity.
rows.measure: Training and validation accuracy over training
rows.baseline: N = 1 setting; exact trajectory values not stated
rows.value: Validation accuracy spikes before training saturation; increased visual diversity significantly reduces the generalization lag.
rows.note: The stated validation-before-training-saturation order is opposite to the post-saturation delay specified in V1.
rows.check: Not 'reversed'. The authors still call N = 4 grokking: 'grokking remains feasible at N = 4'. Figure 9 is captioned as 'synchronized convergence' with a reduced lag. That is a weakened delay, not generalization preceding memorization in the opposite sense. Also, N varies the number of images per class, not the operand-pair training fraction that V1's dataset-size clause refers to.

rows.subject: single-layer DiT
rows.operation_detail: Train with smaller patches and track grokking dynamics.
rows.value: Smaller patches prolong overfitting and delay the grokking point.
rows.note: This varies patchification, not training-set size.
rows.check: State is fine. The row bears on V1's delay only. Patch size is not training-set size, so it says nothing about the dataset-size clause. Its numbers_found entry '1/1' is odd, since no numbers are given.

rows.subject: single-layer DiT with standard SA–FFN architecture
rows.operation_detail: Train the standard architecture in the diverse-image regime.
rows.baseline: FFN-sandwich architecture; exact comparison values not stated
rows.value: The standard SA–FFN baseline failed to trigger grokking; scaling width was insufficient to overcome the failure.
rows.note: Architecture comparison, not a null control.
rows.check: The role should be 'main' (architecture comparison), not 'control'. The text gives no accuracy values, only that SA–FFN 'failed to trigger grokking' even with wider models.

rows.subject: FFN–SA–FFN (FFN-sandwich) diffusion model
rows.operation_detail: Train on image-based modular addition with diverse images per class.
rows.value: The authors describe a grokking pattern consistent with the N = 4 case and report terminal validation accuracy of 94%.
rows.note: The paper reports 94%, not near-perfect accuracy, and states that the standard SA–FFN architecture did not grok in this regime.
rows.check: Appendix D.3 separately reports 95% inference accuracy on the filtered evaluation set. The value should note both figures (94% terminal validation, 95% inference).

relationships.condition: Image-based modular addition, P = 23 EMNIST. Single-layer DiT at N = 1 (S = 32 and S = 16), and standard depth-2 DiT at N = 1 and N = 256.
relationships.reason: Training accuracy saturates while validation stays near chance, then jumps to near-perfect accuracy (r1, r6, r7). Smaller patches lengthen the delay (r3). Delays are read from figures; no step counts are given.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy stayed near chance after training saturation before jumping to near-perfect, and smaller patches lengthened the delay.

source_check.condition: Image-based modular addition, P = 23 EMNIST. Single-layer DiT at N = 1 (S = 32 and S = 16), and standard depth-2 DiT at N = 1 and N = 256.
source_check.reason: Section 4.1 explicitly reports delayed near-perfect generalization; Appendix B reports prolonged overfitting with smaller patches; Appendix K reports grokking in both depth-2 regimes. The training-set-size clause is untested.

relationships.condition: Single-layer models with higher visual diversity per class (N = 4, N = 256).
relationships.reason: At N = 4 the lag shrinks to near-synchronized convergence (r2). At N = 256 the standard SA–FFN fails to grok even when scaled (r4). The FFN-sandwich model plateaus at 94% rather than near-perfect (r5). Grokking here therefore depends on data diversity and architecture.
relationships.display_finding: At N=4, convergence became nearly synchronized; at N=256, scaled SA–FFN models failed to grok and the FFN-sandwich model plateaued at 94%.
